citation.authors: Hussain T, Juraschek SP, Miller ER 3rd, Sacks FM et al

cited_by.title: Caribbean and West African diets and health

record.population: 335 adults with ambulatory blood pressure data in the DASH-Sodium trial, 58% self-reported Black
record.design: Randomised controlled feeding trial of a control diet and DASH diet at three sodium levels
record.finding: Reducing sodium and consuming the DASH diet, alone or combined, significantly lowered 24-hour, awake and asleep blood pressure in Black and non-Black participants.
record.note: DASH is a US-designed pattern, not a Caribbean or West African one.

record.population: 335 adults with ambulatory blood pressure data in the DASH-Sodium feeding trial, 58% self-reported Black
record.design: Randomised controlled feeding trial: control or DASH diet, each at low, intermediate and high sodium for 30 days in random order
record.finding: Compared with the control diet at high sodium, reducing sodium and eating the DASH diet, alone or combined, significantly lowered 24-hour, awake and asleep blood pressure in Black and non-Black participants. The DASH diet with low sodium cut awake systolic pressure by 9.0 mmHg in Black and 7.5 in non-Black participants. Racial differences in achieved levels of asleep pressure persisted.
record.note: Food was supplied in a feeding trial, so it shows what the diet can do, not what people do at home.
